title: Gateway Arch
visualBrief: Weighted catenary shell with equilateral triangular sections, separate steel faces, longitudinal shop welds, field station welds, 32 recessed observation ports and crown service hatch. Entirely editable metric geometry with a shared brushed-stainless surface.

nativeAxes.front: +X is north and +Z is west; the two glazed elevations face east and west
nativeAxes.origin: Ground-level midpoint between the two leg centroids

scaleBasis: NPS published centroid equation and section dimensions. Surface reconstruction yields 192.024 m height and approximately 192.025 m width without independent scaling. Ground plane clips the sloped foot sections.

geographicProposal.evidence: NPS states a north-south leg axis; native +X is north. Anchor currently comes from the candidate identity.
geographicProposal.limitations: Precise leg coordinates, geographic origin and plaza datum require map/site verification. No automatic placement approved.
geographicProposal.notes: NPS states a north-south leg axis; native +X is north. Anchor currently comes from the candidate identity. Precise leg coordinates, geographic origin and plaza datum require map/site verification. No automatic placement approved.

sourceFacts.windowDimensionCaution: NPS fact sheet says 27 inches wide; 2010 HSR says approximately 24 inches. The source uses the fact-sheet external width; clear opening/frame distinction is unresolved.

geometrySource: Original deterministic geometry informed by cited dimensions, measured plans and photographs. No downloaded mesh or photographic texture is embedded.
sourceLicense: Original geometry under repository license. Map-derived outline information is attributed to OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Shared material graphs with metric repeat UV0 and original vertex tints; GLB PBR fallback remains self-contained. No per-model texture duplication.
limitations: Centroid and envelope are dimensionally constrained; construction station positions, window station offsets and service hatch dimensions remain a reconstruction pending original drawing comparison.
Current leg exit surrounds, ground apron and museum entrance are separate unfinished site features. Underground interior is not represented.
Brushed stainless is shared; weld staining, local oil-canning and current cleaning condition require a photographic material pass.
NPS sources differ on window width and count prefabricated segments differently; these discrepancies remain recorded rather than silently harmonized.
Near/far visual QA, shared-material inspection and maximum-fidelity approval remain pending.
